title: Third-Party Sensitive Query Handling Playbook
summary: Playbook for assessing, contracting, and operationalizing third-party handling of sensitive user queries — covers questionnaire items, contract language samples, evidentiary requests, and an escalation matrix for DPA/contract negotiations.
body:
Purpose:
This playbook is intended for security, legal, and product teams to assess and contractually require safe handling of sensitive user queries (e.g., PII, health, financial, or other regulated content) by third-party model-hosting vendors and partners. It focuses on: (1) vendor assessment questions, (2) minimum contractual clauses to include in DPAs/SAAs, (3) empirical evidence requests, (4) operational controls and monitoring expectations, and (5) an escalation and exceptions path for sales/solutions teams.

Scope:
Applies to any external provider that: (a) forwards or persists raw user prompts/queries, (b) processes model outputs on Redwood customers' behalf, or (c) provides managed inference. Not intended to replace full DPA templates but to supplement vendor-specific handling of sensitive queries.

Quick risk summary (one-liner):
Third parties that see or persist raw queries pose medium-to-high risk for regulated workloads unless strong redaction, ephemeral logging, and certified deletion controls are demonstrated.

1) Assessment checklist (questions to ask during onboarding) -- answer options: Yes/No/Partial + short evidence comment
- Data minimization: Can vendor configure the model endpoint to discard raw prompts after inference, and not persist them by default?
- Redaction pipeline: Do you offer a configurable pre-processing redaction filter (customer-controlled rules) that removes/obfuscates PII before the request reaches model weights?
- Default logging posture: Are request/response payloads logged by default? If yes, where (S3, DB, ephemeral memory), and what retention?
- Ephemeral KV handling: If KV caches are used, are prompt prefixes or session tokens persisted beyond the inference lifetime?
- Encryption at rest/in transit: Are both request payloads and cached artifacts encrypted with customer-isolated keys (KMS/HSM)?
- Key separation: Can customers bring and control their KMS keys for any stored artifacts?
- Redaction verifiability: Do you provide deterministic proof (hashes, redact-audit) that redaction rules were applied and which fields were removed?
- Deletion certification: Can vendor produce a signed deletion certificate that lists object IDs, deletion times, and KMS key IDs used?
- Regulated-data training: Does vendor use customer prompts to further train models or fine-tune endpoints? If yes, is explicit opt-in documented?
- Access controls & admin ops: Who within the vendor org can access raw queries? Is access role-based and audited?
- Third-party subprocessors: List subprocessor names that may receive raw queries and provide evidence of their controls.
- Endpoint segmentation: Can you guarantee per-customer isolation of model instances or namespaces to avoid accidental cross-tenant leakage?
- Redaction error handling: If redaction rules malformed a request, what is the fail-safe mode (reject vs send raw)?
- Incident playbook: Does the vendor have a documented incident response playbook for exposed sensitive queries, with SLA for customer notification?

2) Minimum contractual language (clauses to include in DPA/Annex or SAA) -- short, negotiable templates
- Data Minimization Clause: Vendor will not store, index, or otherwise persist customer prompts beyond the minimum required for processing and troubleshooting. Customer may request deletion at any time and receive a deletion certificate within 7 business days.
- Redaction & Preprocessing Clause: Vendor will implement customer-configurable redaction rules applied client-side or at the edge prior to transmission to hosted models. Vendor must provide a manifest of redaction rule versions used for customer traffic for audit.
- Ephemeral Logging & Forensics Clause: Vendor shall only retain request/response payloads for troubleshooting for a maximum of X days (negotiable), after which data is irretrievably deleted. Any retained logs shall remain encrypted under customer-managed keys where requested.
- No Derivative Training Clause: Vendor agrees not to use customer prompts, outputs, or derivative representations for model training, benchmarking, or improvement unless explicit written consent is provided and a commercial agreement for training-use is established.
- Subprocessor Transparency & Flow-down Clause: Vendor will provide a current list of subprocessors and ensure contractual flow-down of equivalent data handling obligations.
- Deletion Certification & Audit Rights: Upon customer request, vendor will provide signed deletion certificates and evidence of deletion. Customer retains the right to engage a third-party auditor under NDA once per 12 months.
- Escrow & Incident Notification Clause: For breaches that expose sensitive queries, vendor commits to notify the customer within 24 hours with technical details and provide remediation timelines.

3) Evidence & artifacts to request during review (concrete deliverables)
- Architecture diagram showing where raw prompts traverse the vendor stack (ingress, preprocessing, caching, model runtime, logging, analytics).
- Sample redaction rule set and versions, plus a short recording or trace of a single request showing redaction applied.
- S3/DB bucket names (or types) where logs are stored, retention policies, and an example object lifecycle rule.
- KMS key identifiers and key rotation policy; confirmation whether keys are customer-provided or vendor-managed.
- Role-based access list (redacted) showing which engineering, ops, and support roles can access raw payloads and an example of audit logs showing access events.
- Deletion certificate template and a recent example produced for another customer (sanitized).
- Pen test / pentest scope showing whether web/API/ingress logging and storage were covered in the last 12 months.

4) Operational controls & monitoring recommendations (what Redwood product/ops should require)
- Default opt-out: The vendor's default config for Redwood customer accounts must be non-persistent logging and strict minimal retention. Any non-default persistence must be opt-in and documented.
- Canary dataset evals: Require periodic tests where Redwood sends synthetic PII strings through vendor endpoints to verify redaction and retention claims (coordinate with vendor test account).
- Observable metrics: Request per-endpoint retention_count, deleted_object_count, redact_fail_rate exposed via vendor metrics endpoint or CSV export monthly.
- Rollout gating: Solutions/Sales must not enable production customer traffic to any vendor-managed persistent logs until evidence pack delivered and reviewed by sec/compliance.

5) Risk scoring rubric (for rapid decisions)
- Low risk: Vendor proves per-customer KMS, no persistent logs, signed deletion certificates, no training on customer data.
- Medium risk: Vendor offers opt-in KMS, has short default retention (e.g., 7 days) for troubleshooting, limited subprocessor transparency. Needs compensating controls (e.g., aggressive redaction, audit rights).
- High risk: Vendor persists raw prompts indefinitely, trains on customer data, or refuses deletion/audit rights. Escalate to legal + GTM; require additional contractual protections or decline for regulated customers.

6) Negotiation playbook & fallback language (practical pointers)
- Prioritize: (1) no-derivative-training, (2) deletion certificates, (3) KMS control, (4) limited retention. If vendor resists, accept short retention windows and stronger redaction+auditing as compensating controls.
- If vendor uses global buckets: require per-customer path prefixes and server-side encryption with customer key wrapping as minimum.
- If subprocessor refuses flow-down: require express customer notification and ability to terminate subprocessor use for the customer.

7) Sample SLO/SLA snippets to include
- Deletion certificate delivery: 7 business days from request (target 3 days for enterprise customers).
- Incident notification for sensitive query exposure: initial notification within 24 hours, with a full incident report within 5 business days.
- Redaction failure rate: vendor will maintain redact_fail_rate < 0.1% across sampled traffic; monthly reports provided.

8) Escalation matrix (who to loop in at Redwood)
- Sales/Deal lead: raise to Solutions Eng 
- If vendor refuses deletion/keys: Security (Laura Chen) + Legal (Data Privacy counsel) -> escalate to VP of Product for commercial decision.
- If vendor constitutes high risk for a regulated customer: immediate stop to onboarding and require exec sign-off.

9) Example template: Short clause to paste into SAA (editable)
"Vendor will not retain or use customer prompts, completions, or derived artifacts for any purpose other than providing the contracted service to Customer. Vendor shall apply Customer-configured redaction rules prior to any storage or downstream processing. All stored artifacts shall be encrypted under Customer-managed KMS keys when requested. Vendor will provide deletion certificates within 7 business days and permit one annual third-party audit under NDA to verify deletion and non-training claims."

Open questions & TODOs:
- Define standard redact_fail_rate measurement method (sampling size, sampling frequency).
- Finalize enterprise deletion SLA tiers (standard vs premium).
- Create a lightweight vendor attestation template to collect initial yes/partial/no answers programmatically.

Appendix: quick negotiation checklist for AE/SE (copyable into deal playbook)
- Ask: Do you persist raw prompts by default? (if yes -> request immediate evidence pack)
- Ask: Can we apply our redaction rules? (if no -> raise to security)
- Ask: Will you use our KMS for stored artifacts? (if no -> negotiate or require deletion certificate policy)
- Ask: Do you ever train on customer data? (if yes -> require written consent flow and commercial terms)

End of playbook.

Notes to reviewer: This is an onboarding-playbook-style doc intended for pragmatic deal flow and security reviews (lighter than a full DPA annex). Request feedback on the evidence checklist and redact_fail_rate definition; want to convert into a short Google Form/attestation in Q1 2026.
